This course follows the 18-lecture sequence of BIOC 1420: Introductory Biochemistry for Nursing Students (Dalhousie University, Winter 2025). The lecture order, unit boundaries, and assessment weights below come from that syllabus.

Each lecture page gives you the objectives, the core facts, and a self-check. The interactive visual explainer carries the pictures and animations; use it alongside the lecture pages rather than reading the course end to end.

What to know

  • Unit 1 · Foundations and proteins — lectures 1–5: fundamental concepts, proteins, protein structure and binding, enzymes, protein applications.
  • Unit 2 · Carbohydrate metabolism — lectures 6–9: carbohydrates, glycogen and glycolysis, the TCA cycle, electron transport and oxidative phosphorylation.
  • Unit 3 · Lipids — lectures 10–12: lipid structure, beta oxidation and lipid metabolism, lipid-centered applications.
  • Unit 4 · Energy, nutrition and information — lectures 13–18: ATP management, nutrition, DNA, transcription and translation, DNA and RNA applications.
  • Assessment in BIOC 1420 — weekly online quizzes 10% (best 8 of 10), midterm 1 25%, midterm 2 25%, final 35%; the highest exam is raised by 5%. Use the checks here as low-stakes practice, not as a substitute for the official assessments.

Check

check.question: Which unit of this course covers enzymes and protein structure?
check.explanation: Lectures 2–5 move from amino acids and protein shape to enzymes and protein-centered applications, all inside Unit 1.
